I got a 144hz monitor recently. Specifically, the BenQ XL2411Z. While the difference between 144hz and 60hz is mind-blowing in its immersive effects, 60FPS isn't nearly as bad compared to it as 30 FPS is compared to 60. Playing USF4 is still fine, even though I'm getting used to playing games such as Rocket League (with cap disabled) and CS:GO at 144hz.

The way I understand it, 4k makes it look better, while 144 Hz makes it feel better.

4k means you've got quadruple the pixels to render, allowing for more high-quality images to be displayed on the screen. It also means (IIRC) about a 4 times increase in how hard a graphics card will work for the same framerate.

144 Hz means you've got a little over double the frames to work with, so you can often react faster and see what your reactions lead to faster. Since it's about 2.5 times as many frames, the graphics card would work about 2.5 times as much (IIRC) to push the same resolution.

Also, IPS all the way, if Linus (of Linus Tech Tips) is right. IPS is more expensive, but has far better viewing angles and color reproduction. The only downside (minus price) is that the response time is lower. This is all going off of Linus's Techquickie video, since I'm not a monitor expert.

Basically, it just comes down to what you're looking for. Do you want even better looking visuals, or do you want to have your games feel and look extremely smooth?
Unless V-sync is on, your GPU works at the same rate. If you would get over 144fps in a game normally, the monitor won't increase your GPU's workload.
As others have said I would recommend the alternative 1440p with 144hz. A lot of programs have scaling issues with 4k and I don't know if windows 10 fixes them. Oh and IPS over TN anytime.
